description: Men's college soccer recruiting research: NCAA D1/D2, NAIA and U SPORTS programs.
caveats: Enrolment figures are approximate and not drawn from official fact books.
Coaching staffs change frequently. Verify before contacting.
Several schools still need a coach-contact sweep.
Kennesaw State is a partial profile: the program exists but no public staff information could be retrieved.

schools.name: SMU
schools.summary: Defending ACC champions, and the one big-name school where CS isn't gated.
schools.verdict: Blue-chip soccer, elite teaching ratios, unrestricted CS. The cost is the barrier at nearly $70,000.
program_notes: Founded 1975. Fourth head coach in program history; Hudson is 115-44-23 across 11 seasons.
Won the first ACC tournament title in program history in 2025 and opened 2026 at 5-0-1, ranked No. 7.
37 NCAA appearances, College Cups in 2000 and 2005, Elite Eights in 2010, 2019 and 2024.
The 2023 side produced four All-Americans — most of any Division I program that year.
Washburne Stadium, capacity 2,577. Dedicated soccer venue, ten home matches.
academic_notes: 11:1 ratio, average class size 22, 70% of classes at 25 or fewer. Best-in-class teaching for a school this size.
Cox School of Business ranked #25 nationally — but direct-admit, so you must name business as your primary interest on the application.
Computer science is not a restricted major. A real edge over Penn State, Ohio State, UCSB and NJIT, which all gate it behind a second application.
geography_notes: Not a college town. 234 walkable acres in University Park, an affluent enclave inside Dallas.
Two airports: Love Field 15 minutes, DFW 30–35. Strong routing for a Canadian family.
Residential Commons system, two years on campus required.
schools.known_for: George W. Bush Presidential Center is on campus. Peruna, a live Shetland pony, is the mascot. Only school ever given the NCAA death penalty (football, 1987).

schools.name: UCF
schools.questionnaire: Recruit Questionnaire in the men's soccer nav
schools.summary: Reigning Sun Belt champions who beat Kentucky and Marshall on the road to get there.
schools.verdict: Cheap, warm, winning, and one flight from Toronto. The class sizes are the honest cost.
program_notes: Calabrese is in his 10th season. Won the first Sun Belt tournament title in program history in 2025.
That run was entirely away: 3-2 in 2OT at Georgia Southern, 1-0 at top-seeded Kentucky, then Marshall — the Herd's first home loss in 721 days.
In their first-ever Sun Belt match (2023) they won 2-1 at then-No. 9 Clemson. Clemson won the national title that year.
Built on the back line. Preseason All-Sun Belt: GK Matisse Hébert (preseason Goalkeeper of the Year), defender Takahiro Fujita (second straight preseason Defensive POY), defender Jem Hewlett.
Round of 16 in 2019 and 2020. Twelve NCAA appearances.
academic_notes: Largest university in Florida — 70,674 students, 59,649 undergraduates.
The trade-off is scale: 28:1 ratio, only 28% of classes under 20 students. The inverse of SMU.
Out-of-state is $24,076, roughly a third of SMU. Verify international rates separately.
geography_notes: 1,420 acres, 13 miles east of downtown Orlando. Large and spread out, ringed by student apartments.
Orlando International is 20–25 minutes with direct Toronto service — one of the best air links here.
~12,140 beds on campus, mostly first-years. Huge adjacent rental market.
schools.known_for: Deep ties to the space and simulation industries. Rosen College of Hospitality is nationally leading. Knightro the knight.

schools.name: USF
schools.summary: The strongest MLS pipeline on the list, mid-rebuild with 22 newcomers.
schools.verdict: A brand-new staff rebuilding from scratch is the most open door on the Core 12 — and the most uncertain.
program_notes: USF's oldest varsity program — played the school's first-ever intercollegiate contest on 25 September 1965.
31 MLS draft picks, including two-time Golden Boot winner Jeff Cunningham, World Cup international Roy Wegerle and MLS Cup winner Dom Dwyer.
14 conference tournament titles, 22 NCAA appearances, Elite Eights in 1997, 2008 and 2011.
2026 is a full reset. Kiefer returned in December 2025 for a second tenure and brought in 22 newcomers — eight from Grand Canyon — with only six players returning. Opened 1-3.
Corbett Stadium, capacity 4,000 — largest dedicated venue among the Core 12.
academic_notes: AAU member, ranked #88 nationally — level with SMU and 29 places above UCF.
21:1 ratio. Better than UCF, well short of SMU.
Muma College of Business and the Pippenger School of Accountancy are separately AACSB-accredited — one of only 194 institutions worldwide.
geography_notes: 1,562 acres in north Tampa, ten miles from downtown. Suburban and spread out.
Tampa International 20–25 minutes, consistently rated among the best US airports.
Busch Gardens is adjacent. Gulf beaches 35–45 minutes.
schools.known_for: The Rowdies Cup — the winner keeps the actual 1975 Soccer Bowl trophy until the next meeting. Rocky D. Bull.

schools.name: South Carolina
schools.summary: Ranked No. 6 nationally, and the best crowds in American college soccer.
schools.verdict: A top-six program, the best atmosphere in the country, the top-ranked international business degree, and forgiving admissions. The airport is the only real weakness.
program_notes: 5-0 and ranked No. 6 nationally as of mid-September 2026 — one of only seven unbeaten sides in Division I.
Led the nation in attendance four straight seasons. The Clemson match on 28 August drew 7,671, the largest crowd in program history.
First program to lead attendance four years running since UCSB's 2007–2015 streak.
1993 national runner-up. College Cups in 1988 and 1993, 22 NCAA appearances.
Annan directed the Atlanta United academy before this — a developer, not just a recruiter. He succeeded Mark Berson, who held the job for 43 years.
Stone Stadium, capacity 5,700, known as The Graveyard for the cemetery next door.
academic_notes: Founded 1801, one of the oldest public universities in the US. 19:1 ratio.
Darla Moore's undergraduate International Business program has been ranked No. 1 in the US for 27 consecutive years.
~64% acceptance with an average SAT of 1280 — the most accessible admission of any top-25 program here.
geography_notes: 444 acres in downtown Columbia. The closest thing to a real college town among the Core 12, woven into a city of 140,000.
Weakest air link of the Core 12. Columbia Metropolitan is small; most routing goes via Charlotte or Atlanta. Charlotte Douglas is 90 minutes by car.
~900 miles to the border — the first school where driving is conceivable.
schools.known_for: The Horseshoe, the 1801 campus core. SEC athletics culture — though men's soccer plays in the Sun Belt. Cocky the mascot.

schools.name: Ohio State
schools.summary: Best-balanced school on the list — top-five soccer, top-15 public, three hours from the border.
schools.verdict: If one school has to balance soccer, academics and travel, this is it.
program_notes: Ranked No. 4 and 3-0, outscoring opponents 9-0 and outshooting them 70-14.
No. 1 overall seed in the 2024 NCAA tournament — highest in program history — reaching the College Cup semifinal.
Maisonneuve inherited a 1-15-2 team in 2018 and built this. He played for the Columbus Crew 1996–2004.
Four Big Ten regular-season titles and four tournament titles. 2007 national runner-up.
The 2025 squad posted a team GPA of 3.31 and a United Soccer Coaches Academic Award.
Jesse Owens Memorial Stadium, natural grass, ~4,518 for soccer.
academic_notes: #41 nationally and #15 among publics — highest-ranked school on the Core 12.
14:1 ratio, better than any other large public here. 93% retention.
Computer science is a restricted major — CSE ranks #38 nationally but requires a separate competitive application.
Out-of-state admission runs 35–40%, well below the headline rate. International applicants sit in that harder pool.
geography_notes: A true college town inside a real city. Columbus is the 14th-largest US city, but the university owns its district. High Street runs the length of campus.
Roughly 190 miles to Detroit–Windsor, about 3 to 3.5 hours. By far the best border proximity on the Core 12 — parents can drive to matches.
Two-year live-on requirement backed by one of the largest residence systems in the country.
schools.known_for: Ohio Stadium holds over 100,000. Fisher College of Business. The Wexner Center for the Arts. Brutus Buckeye.

schools.name: Penn State
schools.summary: A Canadian national-championship coach in year one of a rebuild.
schools.verdict: Highest-upside situation on the Core 12. A championship coach who needs players will give minutes — if you can absorb a three-year rebuild.
program_notes: Rob Dow was born in Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia. He will read a Canadian player's background with more context than most.
At Vermont he went 129-41-21, made five consecutive NCAA tournaments and won the 2024 national championship — the only America East coach ever to do it.
Penn State puts him at the ninth-best win percentage among active Division I men's coaches.
He inherited a hard job. Penn State finished last in the Big Ten in each of the past two seasons — 5-8-4 overall, 1-6-3 in conference last year.
The program was strong recently: Big Ten tournament champions in 2019 and 2020, ranked as high as No. 11.
Jeffrey Field. Crowds are modest — a few hundred for conference matches.
academic_notes: #59 nationally, #26 among publics. 7,958 acres, the largest campus here.
89% of faculty are full-time against a 47% national average. But intro courses run in 300-seat lecture halls.
Smeal Business, Engineering and Schreyer Honors are direct-admit and far more selective than the university's headline rate. Computer science sits inside Engineering, so it carries that bar.
geography_notes: The most genuine college town on either list, and the most isolated. State College is 42,000 people existing because of the university.
~250 miles to Buffalo–Niagara, about 4.5 hours. Second-best border access on the Core 12. Toronto is about 6 hours.
University Park Airport is 10 minutes but small, with no direct international service. Pittsburgh is 2.5 hours.
schools.known_for: One of the largest alumni networks in the world. THON, the largest student philanthropy anywhere. Beaver Stadium holds 106,000. The Nittany Lion.

schools.name: Boston University
schools.summary: Best teaching ratio on the list, and the most reachable coaching staff.
schools.verdict: Small classes, real soccer, an easy staff to contact. The price and the admission rate are the gates.
program_notes: The only Patriot League team to reach the semifinals in each of the last four seasons.
2023 was the best season ever: swept the regular season and tournament titles, 12-4-4, first All-America honour in 18 years, an MLS SuperDraft pick.
Regular-season champions in 2023 and 2024. The frustration is two straight 1-0 semifinal losses.
Led the Patriot League in points, goals and assists last season on a 10-8 record.
All four coaches publish direct emails — among the easiest staffs here to approach.
Nickerson Field, capacity 9,871, opened 1915 on the site of Braves Field.
academic_notes: 10:1 student-faculty ratio — the best on the entire Core 12, with 60% of classes under 20 students.
#42 nationally. Questrom School of Business; the College of Communication is among the country's strongest.
Admission is hard: 11.1% for the Class of 2028. Tuition $71,372, the most expensive here.
geography_notes: No traditional quad. The campus runs a mile and a half along Commonwealth Avenue, bisected by the Green Line.
Logan International 20–30 minutes with frequent direct Toronto flights. Best air link alongside Orlando.
~300 miles to Derby Line, Vermont — about 5 hours. Montreal is roughly the same.
schools.known_for: Elite men's ice hockey and the Beanpot. Martin Luther King Jr. earned his doctorate here. Rhett the Boston Terrier.

schools.name: Northeastern
schools.summary: Strongest academics on either list, weakest soccer on the Core 12. That trade is the whole story.
schools.verdict: If soccer is the route into an institution otherwise out of reach, this is the clearest example of that trade anywhere here.
program_notes: The weakest program on the Core 12 by record — all-time 285-387-87, two NCAA appearances ever (2002, 2012).
Bonomo's three seasons have been roughly flat: 4-5-7, 4-7-4, and about 3-2-2 so far.

But his credential is recruiting. At Cincinnati he brought in six top-100 recruits, five high-school All-Americans and two youth internationals. A coach who built his name recruiting answers enquiries.
He won the 2023 Horizon League title at Green Bay — that program's first NCAA berth in over a decade.
Parsons Field is in Brookline, two miles off campus — a daily commute BU players don't have.
academic_notes: 5.2% acceptance rate for the Class of 2028, from roughly 105,000 applications. The most applied-to private university in the United States.
#46 nationally, #5 for Most Innovative, #9 for undergraduate international business. D'Amore-McKim ranked #20; its own admit rate is 6%.
Co-op is the whole proposition: 95.5% of 2025 business graduates completed an internship before graduating; 91.7% employed within three months.
Campuses in Toronto and Vancouver — unique on this list for a Canadian family.
geography_notes: 73 acres in the Fenway district — the most compact urban campus here.
Logan International 20 minutes, frequent direct Toronto service.
~300 miles to Derby Line, Vermont, about 5 hours.
schools.known_for: Khoury College is one of the oldest dedicated computer science colleges in the country. One of the sharpest reputational climbs in American higher education. Paws the husky.

schools.name: UC Santa Barbara
schools.summary: The only national champion here — and the only school that fails the business requirement outright.
schools.verdict: The best soccer pedigree available — unless a business degree is a requirement, in which case it's out.
program_notes: 2006 NCAA national champions, 2004 runners-up. The only national champion on either list.
Over 60 players have gone professional or represented senior national teams — the best conversion rate in this research.
NCAA attendance champions nine straight years, 2007–2015 — the longest streak in the record books. They hold the top six all-time on-campus attendance records.
Peak crowd: 15,896 against UCLA in 2010, a night the fire marshal turned fans away.
Vom Steeg is in his 25th season. Harder Stadium holds 17,000 — the largest venue on either list.
Planning note: UCSB leaves the Big West for the West Coast Conference after 2026–27.
academic_notes: #40 nationally, #14 among publics. 56.5% of classes under 20. 85% four-year graduation — the highest here.
No undergraduate business administration major. Economics & Accounting and Technology Management only. The one hard disqualifier on the Core 12.
Physics is world class — the Kavli Institute, where six Nobel laureates have worked. CS ranks #35 but is a restricted major.
Quarter system, not semesters. And the UC system is test-blind — scores are not considered at all.
geography_notes: Literally on the beach — a bluff above the Pacific with ocean on two sides and a lagoon through the middle.
Isla Vista, the adjacent student town, is one of the densest residential communities in the US — convenient, and with a party reputation worth discussing openly.
Santa Barbara airport is small; LAX is two hours. ~1,200 miles to the border, 18–19 hours.
schools.known_for: Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics. One of the most beautiful campuses in the country. The College of Creative Studies. Michael Douglas is an alumnus.

schools.name: NJIT
schools.summary: Best financial outcome on the Core 12, and the best airport access.
schools.verdict: Best return on investment here, if the subject fit is right and you can finish the degree.
program_notes: America East, with a 17-match slate and ten home games in 2026 — unusually home-heavy.
Opened against Siena, the 2025 MAAC champions and an NCAA tournament side.
The America East is competitive: Vermont won the 2024 national championship out of it.
Small-crowd college soccer — adult tickets are $10.
Three of four coaches publish direct emails.
academic_notes: Median salary six years after graduation is $69,591 — the highest on the Core 12. IU Indianapolis is $47,173.
#80 nationally, #34 for social mobility. Money rated it the top public university in New Jersey.
65% acceptance but only a 51% four-year graduation rate — easy to enter, hard to finish.
Narrow by design. An engineering and computing institute. CS is a restricted major. Wrong school if interests might shift to humanities.
geography_notes: 48 dense urban acres in Newark's University Heights — the smallest campus on the Core 12, crossable in ten minutes.
Newark Liberty International is 10–15 minutes with frequent direct Toronto flights — the best airport access on the Core 12.
Manhattan is 20–30 minutes by PATH train. A world city on a commuter ticket.
schools.known_for: Engineering, computing and architecture. Strong social mobility outcomes. A rigorous, no-frills, career-focused environment. The Highlander.

schools.name: UMass Lowell
schools.summary: Easiest door on the Core 12, and closer to the border than either Boston school.
schools.verdict: The value and access play. Modest soccer, cheap housing, and a realistic drive home.
program_notes: The most modest soccer proposition on the Core 12 — little NCAA history, lower half of a competitive America East.
Where it competes is access: the easiest Core 12 school for both a roster spot and admission.
Every coach publishes a direct email and phone number — one of only six programs here that does.
Cushing Field Complex.
academic_notes: 83% acceptance — by far the most accessible on the Core 12. Test-optional; only 27% of admits submitted scores.
Average net price $18,281, so the $37,460 sticker substantially overstates what most pay.
44% four-year graduation, second-lowest here. Median salary $61,467 — well above IU Indy, below NJIT.
Plastics engineering is close to unique in American higher education. Manning School of Business covers the business requirement.
geography_notes: A former mill city on the Merrimack, 30 minutes north of Boston. Campus splits across three sites connected by shuttle.
~200–230 miles to Derby Line, about 3.5 to 4 hours — better placed for a drive north than BU or Northeastern, and third-best on the Core 12.
Logan is 45 minutes; Manchester, New Hampshire is 35. Housing is markedly cheaper than Boston.
schools.known_for: Engineering, particularly plastics and materials. Division I ice hockey is the flagship sport. Rowdy the River Hawk.

schools.name: IU Indianapolis
schools.summary: A defensive side that scores from penalties — ideal for a defender, a question mark for a forward.
schools.verdict: Cheapest option with the second-best teaching ratio. The graduation and earnings numbers are the honest counterweight.
program_notes: Keegan Boom was elevated to head coach in June 2026. Entirely new staff, actively recruiting.
Opened 2026 with three consecutive 1-0 wins over Lindenwood, Bowling Green and an unbeaten Southern Indiana.
Freshman goalkeeper Peter Field ran a 0.50 goals-against average with three shutouts. Three defenders played every minute of all three matches.
But three of four goals came from penalties, with one from open play. This is a defensively organised side that hasn't solved attacking.
Great fit for a defender or keeper. Forwards should ask directly how they intend to create chances.
All three coaches publish direct emails. Michael A. Carroll Stadium.
academic_notes: 13:1 ratio — second-best on the Core 12, behind only BU. Notable for a school ranked #192.
Cheapest on the Core 12: in-state $10,762, and an average net price of $11,577 — the lowest here.
39% four-year graduation and $47,173 median salary — both the lowest on the Core 12. Largely a commuter population.
Kelley School of Business carries the Indiana University brand. IU School of Medicine is on campus.
geography_notes: 539 acres immediately west of downtown Indianapolis, walking distance to the city centre.
Indianapolis International is 20 minutes. ~350 miles to Detroit–Windsor, 5 to 5.5 hours — fourth-best here.
Historically commuter. Ask directly where the team actually lives.
schools.known_for: Health sciences and the IU School of Medicine. Indianapolis is a serious sports city — the Indy 500, NCAA headquarters. Jawz the Jaguar.

schools.name: FIU
schools.summary: Cheapest out-of-state tuition in the entire research, by a wide margin.
schools.verdict: If cost is a live constraint, this reshapes the list. Verify international rates separately.
program_notes: Two NCAA Division II national championships (1982, 1984) and D2 runners-up twice more. Moved to D1 in 1987.
Division I national runners-up in 1996. Eight D1 NCAA appearances.
Coming off a second consecutive American Conference Championship appearance, third in four seasons.
Three preseason All-Conference players return: forwards Pasquale Capriati and Johan Helan, defender Alfonso Gilleard-Soriano.
Note the conference: FIU plays men's soccer in the American, not Conference USA, despite being a C-USA member in other sports.
academic_notes: Out-of-state tuition $18,964 — the cheapest of any school in this research. NC State at $33,993 is next.
Ranked #1 in the United States for social mobility, #97 nationally. 74% six-year graduation.
22–24:1 ratio; intro classes are lecture-sized. CS ranks #106, engineering #97 — solid rather than elite.
geography_notes: 344 acres in University Park, ten miles west of downtown Miami. Heavily commuter — ~18,000 attend part-time.
Miami International 15–20 minutes with frequent direct Toronto service.
~1,500 miles, about 23 hours — the longest drive of anything on either list.
schools.known_for: Largest Hispanic-serving institution here. Deep Latin American and Caribbean ties. Roary the Panther.

schools.name: Georgia State
schools.summary: Seventeen years of coaching stability and the best airport on either list.
schools.verdict: Buy the coaching stability and the airport. Confirm what campus life actually looks like.
program_notes: Surrency is in his 17th season — since 2010. The coach who signs you will still be there when you graduate.
Three NCAA tournament appearances and a Sun Belt Championship.
All three coaches publish direct emails. Office line 404-413-4002.
The 2026 schedule is punishing: West Virginia, Georgia Southern, South Carolina, Marshall and UCF inside six weeks, plus a preseason trip to Clemson.
Home matches are at Panthersville in Decatur, about 15 minutes from the downtown campus.
academic_notes: #198 nationally but #5 in the United States for Best Undergraduate Teaching. Those measure different things.
Not test-optional — SAT or ACT required for Fall 2026, minimum 480 EBRW / 440 maths, minimum GPA 2.75.
Weakest outcomes here: 33% four-year graduation and $37,844 median salary.
Robinson is the largest business school in the South — 8,000 students, 80,000 alumni.
geography_notes: Not a campus so much as downtown Atlanta. Converted commercial buildings across city blocks, no quad. Primarily a commuter school.
Hartsfield-Jackson — the busiest airport in the world — is 20 minutes by MARTA, with multiple direct Toronto flights daily. The best air connection on either list.
~900 miles to Detroit–Windsor, 13–14 hours.
schools.known_for: Nationally studied for raising graduation rates and closing achievement gaps. Pounce the Panther.

schools.name: Kennesaw State
schools.head_coach: Not found — call the athletics department
schools.summary: Program confirmed to exist, but no public information about it. Phone them.
schools.verdict: Cheap and confirmed, but unknowable from a desk. Low priority until you've spoken to someone there.
program_notes: The program exists — ESPN carries a full 2026 men's soccer schedule and KSU fields 18 Division I teams.
Everything else is unavailable. No head coach name, no record, no conference detail, no staff contact could be retrieved. Searches are swamped by football and basketball.
Go to ksuowls.com directly or telephone the athletics department. The one school here where desk research doesn't work.
Context: athletics is ascendant. Football won the 2025 C-USA title and basketball the 2026 C-USA tournament.
Home matches are likely at Fifth Third Stadium, capacity 10,200.
academic_notes: 24% four-year graduation rate — the worst figure anywhere in this research. Raise it directly with a coach; athletes often graduate at better rates.
#373 nationally, the lowest-ranked school on either list.
Out-of-state $22,278 — second cheapest here after FIU. Around 68–69% acceptance.
Coles College of Business takes ~20% of the entire student body; ranked #104 nationally.
geography_notes: 570 acres across two sites in Cobb County, 25–30 miles northwest of Atlanta. Green, with a lake and nature preserve.
Atlanta's airport is 45–60 minutes away — on the far side of the metro, unlike Georgia State's 20.
Houses 5,000+ students, but that's a small share of 43,000 undergraduates.
schools.known_for: Rapid growth from a junior college. Coles College of Business. Scrappy the Owl.

schools.name: NC State
schools.summary: 2025 national runners-up, picked first in the ACC, and cheaper than most of the Core 12.
schools.verdict: Arguably the best soccer-per-dollar on the whole list, with Boston-level internship density next door.
program_notes: Reached the 2025 NCAA national championship match — the first title-game appearance in program history.
Picked first in the 2026 ACC preseason coaches poll. Opened ranked No. 2, since slipped to around No. 20.
Hubbard's trajectory is extraordinary: Sweet Sixteen and a No. 14 finish in year one, the national final in year two.
Heavy turnover — 15 returners, 18 newcomers including 10 transfers.
Both the 2026 ACC finals and the College Cup are at Cary, twenty minutes from campus. A home-region championship weekend nobody else gets.
Dail Soccer Field, capacity 3,000; the 2025 UNC match drew over 5,000.
academic_notes: Out-of-state tuition $33,993 — lower than every private school here and most of the Core 12, at a #64-ranked university.
15:1 ratio, 68% four-year graduation — far above UMass Lowell or IU Indy.
Poole College ranked #9 nationally among publics for business analytics, but it is one of the most competitive admissions units at NC State.
Wilson College of Textiles is essentially unique in American higher education.
geography_notes: 2,137 acres southwest of downtown Raleigh, adjacent to Research Triangle Park — SAS, Red Hat, IBM, Cisco, Lenovo, GSK.
Raleigh-Durham International 20 minutes with direct Air Canada service to Toronto.
~700 miles to Buffalo–Niagara, about 11 hours.
schools.known_for: Engineering, textiles and veterinary medicine. The 1983 basketball championship. Mr. and Mrs. Wuf.

schools.name: UNC Chapel Hill
schools.summary: The best combination of soccer and academics anywhere here — and the hardest door to open.
schools.verdict: Worth pursuing precisely because athletics is the one route in. Have the admissions conversation with the staff before investing.
program_notes: Two national championships (2001, 2011), a 2008 runner-up finish, nine College Cups, 32 NCAA appearances.
In 79 seasons the program has had only two losing years.
Somoano won the 2011 title in his first year as a head coach — only the second rookie head coach in NCAA history — taking the ACC regular season, ACC tournament and national title in one year.
He has coached two National Players of the Year, 19 All-Americans and 36 MLS SuperDraft or homegrown players.
Signed a three-year extension in April 2026 — no succession risk.
Every coach publishes a direct email, unusual at this level.
academic_notes: #22 nationally, #4 among publics. 14:1 ratio, 97% retention, 92% six-year graduation — the best academic figures in this research.
North Carolina law caps non-resident enrolment at 18%, and the out-of-state acceptance rate runs around 8% — harder than Cornell. 97% of enrolled first-years had a weighted GPA of 4.0+.
Ask admissions how international students count against the 18% cap. It changes the odds materially.
Recruited-athlete admission is a separate process. That's the only realistic route, which makes the soccer conversation matter more here than anywhere.
Kenan-Flagler ranked #8 nationally for undergraduate business — highest general business ranking on either list.
geography_notes: A genuine college town. Chapel Hill is 60,000 people built around the university; Franklin Street is the spine.
Raleigh-Durham International 25 minutes, direct Air Canada to Toronto.
~700 miles to the border, about 11 hours.
schools.known_for: First public university in the United States. Basketball above all. The Anson Dorrance women's dynasty — 21 national titles. Rameses, a live ram.

schools.name: UNC Charlotte
schools.summary: Possibly the strongest value combination in the entire research.
schools.verdict: A winning program, forgiving admission, low cost, ten hours from home, direct flights. The only gap is the blocked staff directory.
program_notes: Reigning American Conference regular-season champions, picked first for 2026.
Back-to-back conference tournament titles in 2023 and 2024, beating FIU in overtime in the 2024 final.
2011 national runners-up — the first team in any sport in school history to reach an NCAA final. 17 NCAA appearances.
Swept the conference's individual awards last season — Goalkeeper, Midfielder and Freshman of the Year. Fisher and Manufor both return, with leading scorer Elias Arsvoll.
Four of six graduating seniors signed professional contracts after 2025; two were MLS draft picks.
Langan has been on staff since 2009. Six of the program's ten conference titles are his.
academic_notes: ~80% acceptance at $22,274 out-of-state — third cheapest here. Average net price $15,018.
#143 nationally, #38 Most Innovative, Carnegie R1.
The first School of Data Science in the Carolinas, and the only BS in Sports Analytics in the Southeast. That combination exists nowhere else on this list.
Belk is the largest business school in North Carolina, top 25% nationally. Every student is guaranteed access to an internship.
geography_notes: 1,000 acres in University City, nine miles from uptown. The LYNX Blue Line runs directly from campus into the city centre.
Charlotte Douglas 25–30 minutes with direct Toronto service.
~650 miles to Buffalo–Niagara, about 10 hours — the shortest in the Carolinas or Georgia.
schools.known_for: Charlotte is the second-largest banking centre in the US. Niche named this the most beautiful public campus in the country. Norm the Niner.

schools.name: Florida Atlantic
schools.summary: Lowest net price in the research, attached to a program that just broke through.
schools.verdict: Cheapest realistic option once aid is counted, on a rising program that recruits Canadians. Contacts still need gathering.
program_notes: 2025 was the first NCAA tournament appearance in 45 years of the program's existence. They won the American Conference tournament and finished 12-4-2.
Currently ranked around No. 19 nationally.
Worthen has been head coach since February 2017 — the breakthrough came in his ninth season, which usually makes it more durable.
New assistant Lucas Champenois has developed 20+ professional players, including a Sporting Kansas City first-round pick. Fluent in French.
FAU's roster has carried Canadian players — a real signal the staff recruits north of the border.
FAU Soccer Stadium holds 1,000 — the smallest venue on either list. No atmosphere.
academic_notes: Average net price $8,636 — the lowest of any school in this research. Out-of-state tuition $21,655.
#183 nationally, #30 for social mobility. Carnegie R1.

Honest caveat: student reviews of the engineering college split sharply — some cite careers at IBM and Cisco, others describe course-availability and advising problems. Probe this with current students.
24:1 ratio, 50% four-year graduation.
geography_notes: 850 acres in affluent Boca Raton, two miles from the Atlantic. Housing is expensive by Florida standards.
Two airports: Fort Lauderdale 30 minutes and Palm Beach 25. FLL carries heavy direct Toronto and Montreal traffic.
~1,450 miles, about 22 hours.
schools.known_for: The 2023 basketball Final Four run put the school on the map. Ocean and coastal research. Owlsley the Owl.

schools.name: Clemson
schools.summary: The best professional pathway in college soccer right now.
schools.verdict: If professional soccer is the goal and $60,000 is absorbable, this is the strongest case anywhere. If not, Charlotte gives you most of it for a third.
program_notes: Four national championships — 1984, 1987, 2021 and 2023 — plus runner-up finishes in 1979 and 2015 and ten College Cup semifinals.
Founded 1934. The oldest and most decorated program in this research. 38 NCAA appearances.
In 2025 Clemson led every NCAA program in the country with four first-round MLS SuperDraft selections. Kwaku Agyabeng became the tenth Tiger to sign a Generation adidas contract.
Reached the ACC championship game in five of the past six seasons.
2025 was a down year at 8-6-3 — and they still won the ACC tournament. That tells you how high the floor is.
Historic Riggs Field, capacity 6,500, with 486 home wins across 60 years. Noonan is in his 17th season; Jones has 14, Rodriguez 11.
academic_notes: Median earnings $75,142 four years after graduation — the highest figure in this research, and measured at four years while NJIT's $69,591 is at six.
#75 nationally. 86–87% six-year graduation, second only to UNC.
Out-of-state cost of attendance now exceeds $60,000 a year, with only 34% receiving need-based aid. Roughly three times FAU.
Computer science ranks #83. Creative Inquiry undergraduate research is the distinctive academic feature.
geography_notes: A small college town of 17,000 on Lake Hartwell at the foot of the Blue Ridge. The most scenic setting here.
Airports are poor. Greenville-Spartanburg is regional with no Toronto service; Charlotte and Atlanta are both two hours by car.
~800 miles, 12–13 hours. First-year students must live on campus.
schools.known_for: Football and Death Valley. Engineering, business and agricultural sciences. The Tiger.

schools.name: Georgia Southern
schools.summary: Easiest admission in the research, attached to a team that was ranked sixth nationally.
schools.verdict: Ranked sixth in the country last year and you can get in with an 88% admit rate. The open question is whether 2025 was a step change or a spike.
program_notes: 2025 was a dramatic breakout: 13-4-1, ranked as high as sixth nationally. The win over Marshall is the biggest in program history.
Head coach Lee Squires is English — born in Sheffield, with a career record of 142-67-31 across three programs.
All four coaches publish direct emails, plus an ARMS questionnaire. One of the easiest staffs to approach.
But there's almost no history behind it. Before 2025 the entire honours list was two conference regular-season titles, in 1990 and 2016.
2026 has started unevenly at roughly 2-1-1, including 0-2 at UNC Wilmington.
The schedule is hard by design: Clemson, Marshall, James Madison, West Virginia and UCF.
academic_notes: 88–90% acceptance — the most accessible school on either list.
Median earnings $62,342 four years out — higher than NC State's six-year figure, despite a #343 ranking.
36% four-year graduation, 24–25:1 ratio.
94–95% of students come from Georgia. A Canadian would be genuinely unusual here — weigh the culture fit honestly.
geography_notes: A classic small Southern college town of 33,000, an hour inland from Savannah. First-years must live on campus.
Airport is poor — Savannah is regional with no Toronto service; Jacksonville 2.5 hours, Atlanta 3.5.
~950 miles, about 15 hours. Also has a campus in Wexford, Ireland.
schools.known_for: Six FCS football national championships. Adrian Peterson and Matt Breida came through. GUS the Eagle.

schools.name: Nova Southeastern
schools.summary: A heavily international squad — but a small undergraduate college inside a health-professions university.
schools.verdict: The international roster is a real positive. Everything else points elsewhere unless marine science appeals.
program_notes: NCAA Division II, Sunshine State Conference — one of the strongest D2 leagues in the country.
2025: 8-4-3, opening with a 2-0 upset of No. 5 Clayton State. Picked fifth for 2026.
Santiago Hoyos Lopez earned First Team All-SSC and ranked sixth nationally in points per game.
The roster is the story: Dahl, Valdez, Morral Rosales, Rokseth, Scerbo, Bulloch, Katsuma, Ricardo. Scandinavian, Spanish, Japanese, British, Latin American. This staff recruits abroad as routine.
D2 scholarships are equivalency-based — partial awards, stackable with academic and need aid.
McArthur is young, promoted in January 2025.
academic_notes: Undergraduate enrolment is only 7,311 — about SMU's size. The ~21,000 figure is two-thirds graduate and professional students.
It does not really meet the 18,000 size criterion.
16:1 ratio — the upside of a small undergraduate college. #257 nationally, 55% four-year graduation.

A student reviewer states the institution prioritises the medical school and advises against enrolling for business. One voice, but consistent with the structure. Weakest academic fit among the extras for your subjects.
geography_notes: 314 suburban acres in Davie, car-dependent. Residence halls only at the Fort Lauderdale campus.
Fort Lauderdale International 20 minutes with heavy direct Toronto and Montreal traffic.
~1,450 miles, about 22 hours.
schools.known_for: Health professions — medicine, dental, pharmacy, optometry. Marine science and coral reef restoration. Razor the Shark.

schools.name: Keiser
schools.summary: Excellent soccer at a 1,500-student career college. NAIA eligibility rules are the useful part.
schools.verdict: Great soccer, wrong academics. Worth knowing for the NAIA eligibility route more than the school itself.
program_notes: 2025 was outstanding: 16-1-2, winning both the Sun Conference regular season and tournament titles, finishing No. 16 nationally.
11-1 at home and 7-0-1 in conference. Reached the second round of the NAIA National Tournament.
Fifth conference regular-season title, and NAIA opening rounds in seven consecutive seasons. Opened 2026 ranked No. 15.
Oldham is in his 10th season; the staff was named NAIA South Staff of the Year.

NAIA eligibility rules are more flexible than the NCAA's — athletic aid stacks more freely with academic and need-based aid, and there is no 2.3 core-GPA sliding scale. A real parallel path if NCAA eligibility is ever tight.
Correction: an earlier note recorded a 2021 NAIA national title. That could not be verified — the football team won the NAIA title in 2023.
academic_notes: The flagship residential campus has about 1,500 students. The ~20,000 figure is the whole system — 21 Florida campuses plus online, China and Nicaragua.
Does not meet the 18,000 criterion in any meaningful sense.
Founded 1977 as a career college. Effectively open admission at 96–97%. Top 25 for social mobility four years running.
Maths and physics almost certainly don't exist as majors. Computing is IT-oriented. Of your four subjects, it meets one.
geography_notes: 100-acre residential campus off Okeechobee Boulevard, built deliberately for a traditional campus experience.
Palm Beach International 15 minutes; Fort Lauderdale 45 with heavy Toronto service.
~1,400 miles, about 21 hours.
schools.known_for: Florida's largest private non-profit by system enrolment. Career education in health and business. The Seahawks.

schools.name: UNC Wilmington
schools.summary: The clearest evidence anywhere that freshmen actually play.
schools.verdict: If early minutes matter more than the badge, this is the strongest evidence on the list. Check the international tuition first.
program_notes: In 2024 Heaney took a roster with 20 combined freshmen and sophomores to the CAA Championship Game.

The goals in that run came from first-year players — Acevedo, D'Amico and Gyamfi. A redshirt freshman goalkeeper kept a clean sheet in the semifinal; a redshirt sophomore saved three penalties in the shootout that won round one.
No other program here demonstrates that pattern so explicitly. Most say freshmen get minutes; this one built a conference final on them.
Heaney is in his 26th season — second-longest tenure in this research after Vom Steeg. 208 wins, four NCAA appearances.
They punch up: a road win at South Carolina and a draw with a ranked Clemson in 2023; beat Georgia Southern 2-0 this season.
academic_notes: #198 nationally but #58 for Best Undergraduate Teaching. 17:1 ratio, average class size ~25.
Cost flag: out-of-state is $25,420, but reported international undergraduate tuition is around $42,603 — a gap of roughly $17,000 a year. Verify before treating this as affordable.
Marine biology is world class, with a waterfront Center for Marine Science and a PhD program.
Not STEM-forward. Maths and physics are small departments. Median salary $46,972.
geography_notes: Between the Cape Fear River and the Atlantic. Wrightsville Beach is ten minutes away and students bike to it.
Airport is weak — Wilmington International is small; Raleigh-Durham is two hours by car.
~750 miles, about 12 hours. All first-years must live on campus.
schools.known_for: Marine biology and coastal research. Film studies, supported by Wilmington's production industry. Sammy C. Hawk.

schools.name: UNC Greensboro
schools.summary: Ranked last by size, and one of the four or five best soccer programs in this entire research.
schools.verdict: The biggest mismatch here between soccer quality and list position. If soccer per dollar is the criterion, this belongs near the top.
program_notes: Five NCAA national championships — 1982, 1983, 1985, 1986 and 1987 at Division III — plus a D2 runner-up finish in 1989.
2025: reached the Sweet Sixteen, beating No. 2 Virginia on penalties to get there. Peaked at No. 11 nationally and stayed in the Top 25 all season.
Two first-round picks in the 2026 MLS SuperDraft — Enzo Dovlo 12th overall to Atlanta United, Issah Haruna 20th to Orlando City. A pipeline that rivals Clemson's.
23 conference regular-season titles, 15 conference tournament titles, 13 D1 NCAA appearances.
Rich has delivered four SoCon regular-season titles and two tournament championships in seven seasons.
UNCG Soccer Stadium, capacity 3,540.
academic_notes: 89–90% acceptance, essentially tied with Georgia Southern as the easiest here.
Average net price $10,907 — second lowest in the research after FAU. Out-of-state tuition $24,014. #13 nationally for social mobility.
Bryan School holds AACSB accreditation in both business and economics — top 1% of business schools worldwide.
Counterweights: 39% four-year graduation and $39,869 median salary, second lowest here. Maths, physics and CS are small departments.
geography_notes: 266 urban acres in a city of 300,000, anchoring the Piedmont Triad.
Sits between Charlotte and Raleigh — 90 and 75 minutes — putting UNC, NC State, Duke and Charlotte all within reach.
Piedmont Triad International is 15 minutes; Charlotte Douglas 90 minutes with direct Toronto service. ~700 miles, about 11 hours.
schools.known_for: Founded 1891 as a women's college. Education, nursing and the performing arts. The Weatherspoon Art Museum. Spiro the Spartan.

schools.name: University of Toronto
schools.summary: The oldest program in this research, in a rebuild year with nine starters gone.
schools.verdict: The strongest academic institution available at domestic prices, mid-rebuild, with a coach openly looking to younger players.
program_notes: Founded 1879 — 147 years ago. By far the oldest program here, predating Clemson by more than half a century.
51 OUA provincial championships, an all-time conference record, plus the 1988 national title and 17 national championship appearances.

2025: won the 51st OUA title 2-0 over York, led the OUA with 42 goals and conceded a province-low eight. The women won their first title the same year — a joint sweep managed only three times before in OUA history.

Orlov has the most internationally developed coaching background in this document: youth performance coach at FC Union Berlin, internships at Fulham, Feyenoord, Korona Kielce and KuPS. Career record 45-15-12.
He is also head coach of Alliance United FC in League1 Ontario — embedded in the same semi-pro ecosystem an Ontario player already moves through.
2026 is a rebuild. Nine starters gone, roughly 1-1-2 so far including a home loss to TMU. Orlov has said he's most excited to work with the younger players.
Varsity Stadium, capacity 4,000, downtown on the St. George campus.
academic_notes: Canada's largest and highest-ranked university, ~98,000 students across three campuses.
The Program of Study system is the key risk. You're admitted to a faculty, not a major. Computer Science and Rotman Commerce are limited-enrolment and you apply after first year, on first-year marks.
That competition happens after you've enrolled and started playing. Ask Orlov and an academic advisor what happens if grades dip during the season.
Maths and physics are world class — the Fields Institute is here. Large first-year classes and demanding grading are well documented.
Domestic Ontario tuition against Northeastern's $69,289 is the clearest financial argument for the Canadian route.
geography_notes: The most urban campus in this research. St. George occupies central Toronto, walkable throughout, with the subway running through it.
No flights required for home matches. Away fixtures at Queen's, Trent, Nipissing, Ontario Tech, TMU and York are all drivable.
Pearson is 30 minutes; Billy Bishop is downtown.
schools.known_for: Canada's flagship research university — insulin, stem cells. Rotman Commerce, Engineering Science, the Fields Institute. True Blue.

schools.name: York University
schools.summary: Reigning national champions, with a roster built from MLS Next Pro and League1 Ontario.
schools.verdict: If the Canadian route is live at all, this is the first call.
program_notes: York are the reigning U SPORTS national champions. They won the 2025 title and are defending it, chasing a seventh in program history.
They lost the 2025 OUA final 2-0 to Toronto and won the national championship anyway. Different trophies — York holds the bigger one.
Six national championships (1977, 2008, 2010, 2014, 2015, 2025) and seven OUA titles. Five of the nationals are Isacco's.

Isacco played Division I soccer at Maryland — three-time All-ACC first team goalkeeper, team captain in 1992, Canadian Olympic Team. The only coach here who came through the American system and now coaches in Canada.
The roster is a professional pathway: two players from Toronto FC II (MLS Next Pro), plus Vaughan SC in League1 Ontario, TMU Bold, Utah Tech (NCAA D1) and a US junior college.
York Lions Stadium is also home to York United FC in the Canadian Premier League.
Eight coaches on staff — the deepest here. Four publish emails.
academic_notes: Canada's third-largest university, ~55,000 students in north Toronto plus the Glendon bilingual campus.

Schulich School of Business is elite, and its BBA is direct-entry — a competitive admission decision rather than a post-first-year hurdle. Arguably better for an athlete: you know where you stand before you arrive.
Osgoode Hall Law School is among Canada's strongest. Lassonde School of Engineering covers computer science.
Generally less selective and less grade-deflating than U of T — worth weighing against prestige for an athlete balancing a season.
geography_notes: Suburban north Toronto at Keele and Steeles. The TTC Line 1 subway extension runs directly onto campus.
More self-contained and isolated in feel than U of T's downtown campus.
Pearson is 25 minutes. No flights for home matches; all OUA away fixtures drivable.
schools.known_for: Schulich and Osgoode Hall. Canada's most successful modern men's university soccer program. Yeo the Lion.

schools.name: Western University
schools.summary: Best traditional campus of the three — but the head coach runs two programs at once.
schools.verdict: Best campus experience of the three. The divided coaching role and the two-year Ivey pathway are the questions to resolve.
program_notes: Painter coaches both the men's and women's teams. At every other school in this research the men's program has a dedicated head coach. Ask how his time is divided and who runs men's training daily.
He is genuinely decorated: U SPORTS Coach of the Year 2013, OUA West Coach of the Year 2013 and 2017, Canada Soccer A License.
With the women since 2012: five OUA West titles, nine straight playoff appearances, five U SPORTS national championship appearances. Took over the men in 2018 and won OUA bronze that first season.
He played four seasons for Western, winning three OUA championships and the 1999 national title — an alumnus and a national champion as a player.
Coached FC London from its 2009 inception through 2015 in the PDL, winning a North American championship in 2012.
Western won OUA titles in 1998 and 2004 and is one of only three programs ever to sweep both men's and women's OUA titles in a season.
academic_notes: ~40,000 students in London, a city of 425,000 two hours from Toronto.
Known for the strongest undergraduate student experience of the Ontario schools — genuinely residential, in a way neither U of T nor York is.

Ivey is an Advanced Entry Opportunity: you apply to another faculty, complete two years, and enter Ivey in third year. AEO status is granted at admission but does not guarantee entry — you must hold marks through years one and two.
Same structural risk as U of T's Program of Study, spread across two years instead of one.
geography_notes: The most traditional campus of the three Canadian options — green, residential, Gothic Revival stone. Closer in feel to Penn State or Clemson.
Under two hours to the Detroit–Windsor crossing, the closest of the three.
London International for regional connections; Pearson about two hours by car.
schools.known_for: Ivey Business School. The strongest undergraduate campus culture in Ontario. Medicine and engineering. JW the Mustang.

no_program.reason: Cut 26 May 2020 in COVID budget reductions, immediately after an 11-7-1 season ranked 69th of 206 in RPI. Never reinstated. The former coach founded Appalachian FC, now in USL League Two, playing at the old stadium.
Club only. The SEC does not sponsor men's soccer — only Kentucky and South Carolina field teams, both as Sun Belt affiliates.
No varsity team. Purdue FC is player-run.
16 varsity teams, seven men's, no men's soccer.
